system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents are treated as the counterparty's untrusted draft.

---

## 0. Process point: the "STANDARD / FINAL / pre-cleared" framing

The Seller's package tries to narrow our review in three ways:

- It says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL".
- It labels most clauses "[STANDARD] … reviewed and cleared by both sides" and asks us to review only "[OPEN]" items. **Nothing is marked [OPEN].**
- It asserts that the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted" and that 10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge bars are "market standard".

**My advice:** None of this binds our review. Under Playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, a position is not agreed, final or cleared because a counterparty document says so. We have no confirmation through our own authority process that any of these points was settled. Amelia Frost has given no written authority on the cap or the claims period. I have therefore reviewed every clause. Each "[STANDARD]" item departs from our playbook in some way.

**Action:** Ask Amelia Frost directly whether any principal-level discussion took place. Tell Seller's counsel that the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are not accepted, and that all clauses remain open.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m; Playbook 25% / AUD 6.0m
- The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback. That fallback is usable **only** with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and we have none. A matching number is not clearance.
- **Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal the fallback.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): Seller AUD 25k de minimis / AUD 250k basket, excess only; Playbook AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar
- The Seller's de minimis is 5x ours and its basket is 5x ours.
- The "excess only" mechanism (a deductible) is a further material departure. Once the basket is exceeded, the Seller would keep the first AUD 250k of every loss.
- The "~1% of price" market claim is an unverified assertion.
- **Push back:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000 as a tipping basket, so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded. Clarify that related claims arising from the same facts aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): Seller 18 months plus a catch-all; Playbook 24 months
- 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The added sentence, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, indemnity and covenant claims into the general limits by default.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the catch-all. Reverse the default so each category has its own expressly stated regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties: Seller wants general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"
- This is a direct conflict with the playbook. Title and capacity are the core of a 100% share purchase. Capping them at 20% would leave us exposed for 80% of the price if title fails.
- **Push back:** Keep a separate Fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- As drafted, these would shield fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. That is our clearest red line, and no one on our side can waive it.
- **Push back:** Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. Also confirm that the exclusive-remedy clause does not cut down the specific indemnities or the Fundamental regime.

### 1.6 Tax / IP: Seller says "settled under the general regime"
- Under our playbook, Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Nothing has been resolved, and we should not assume either unlimited liability or general-regime treatment.
- **Push back:** Reject "settled". Keep Tax and IP as separate categories (including any tax indemnity), to be negotiated on their own terms.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Sched 7)
- Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, which is whole-data-room deemed disclosure.
- Clause 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records", which is public-register deemed disclosure.
- Both are rejected under our playbook. Together they would let the Seller qualify every warranty by anything buried anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012.
- The data room snapshot is dated **22 September 2026**, about six weeks before today (5 November 2026). Facts on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 may have moved since then.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to specific matters in Parts 2 onward that are fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to assess their nature and scope.
  - Disclosure must not qualify Fundamental warranties or specific indemnities.
  - Require an updated disclosure position before signing.

### 2.2 Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admission)
- This is acceptable in principle. Add wording confirming that it does not limit any specific indemnity, Completion deliverable or condition.

### 2.3 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". That is a blanket exclusion, and constructive knowledge on top of it.
- **Push back:** Delete it. If any knowledge concept survives, it should apply only to Seller warranty qualifiers, use named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and Completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%), which makes it a material customer.
- The Seller Update says the consent is "addressed". Its own Disclosure Letter (Part 2) admits **no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. The two documents are inconsistent.
- "Reasonable endeavours" plus "satisfied on delivery of written consent" fails our playbook on both counts.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a Condition Precedent: effective consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, **and** evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - Do not accept consent-on-delivery.
  - Do not accept reasonable endeavours alone. Any obligation should be a firm obligation, backed by a Buyer walk right or long-stop.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and has not been repaid, and no discharge is included (DL Part 3). The facility has change-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions.
- A "release to be provided following Completion" does not meet our playbook. It also sits uneasily with the debt-free / cash-free basis.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter.
  - Require direct repayment to Riverlark out of Completion funds as a funds-flow line, with that amount treated as Debt in the price.
  - Require executed security releases (deeds of release, PPSR discharge undertakings and similar) delivered at Completion.
- Check whether the Riverlark security extends to the sale shares. If it does, this is also a **title / encumbrance** issue.
- A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420,000 left out of the funds flow
- The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. This is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits.
- The bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment, so the Company will pay them after we own it. If they are not in the funds flow, we bear them.
- DL Part 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Push back:**
  - Add a specific funds-flow line, or a Seller-funded mechanism such as a Transaction Expense or Debt deduction or an escrow, covering AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs**.
  - Require the Seller to confirm, or our payroll diligence to quantify, the on-cost amount.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010)
- The Seller says an indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is "adequate". It is too narrow.
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. No payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- The risk is therefore about **IP ownership and infringement**, not just a payment debt.
- The AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 is not independently verified either way. We should not assume it is owed, or that it has been paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or validly use, the Ironquay / SOW3 materials. This includes third-party claims, remediation and re-development.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: verified cleared payment plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and disclosure.

### 4.2 Export / privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sched 6)
- The Seller Update calls this "not expected to be material". Its own Disclosure Letter (Part 6) says the material **does not establish** whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- We should not accept the materiality assessment. Equally, we should not treat this as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Add covenants to preserve all logs and evidence.
  - Require a proper investigation, with the Buyer given regular updates and consultation rights before any regulator or individual communications.
  - Require the Seller to share its findings before Completion.
  - Make sure general disclosure and the knowledge bar do not neutralise the privacy and data warranties for this matter.
  - Revisit protection, such as a specific indemnity or condition, once the facts are known.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; AUD 330k)
- The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own Disclosure Letter says it does **not** state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- The renewals are also described as "related" and to be "read together".
- **Position:** Assess before classifying. Do not assume automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction, and do not accept the Seller's ordinary-course label.
- Request:
  - the contracts;
  - timing relative to Completion and any locked-box or accounts date;
  - termination rights;
  - accrual status;
  - whether "related" means related-party or a single arrangement split into three.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012)
- The Seller relies on its own share register. That is an internal source, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - current ASIC company extract and history;
  - share certificates;
  - constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption or transfer restrictions);
  - PPSR and other encumbrance searches, cross-checked against the Riverlark security;
  - Seller board resolutions and evidence of authority and capacity.
- Title warranties sit in the Fundamental regime (see 1.4).

### 4.5 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller characterises these as a notification obligation only and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's own readings.
- **Action:** Verify against the documents, including any change-of-control definitions. If confirmed, add the lease notification as a Completion deliverable.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Process | "[STANDARD]/FINAL/pre-cleared", review [OPEN] only | Reject. All clauses open. Verify with Amelia Frost. |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar tipping** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months plus "applies to all Claims" | **24 months**. Delete the catch-all override. |
| 4 | Fundamental / Title | Same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket / de minimis / knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | Limits apply to "all Claims" | **Full fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** |
| 6 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Open. Separate categories.** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Delete DL 1.1 / 1.2. Refresh the 22/9 snapshot. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, including advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete.** Named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry only. |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item or Seller-funded** |
| 12 | Ironquay | SOW3-payment indemnity only | **Broaden to IP ownership / infringement. Keep the SOW3 cure.** AUD 180k unverified. |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, provide updates.** No assumed breach or quantum. |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess. No automatic Debt or deduction.** Request facts. |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence** |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification or no consent | **Verify against source documents** |

**Immediate next steps**
1. Send a holding response to Seller's counsel rejecting the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing and confirming that our mark-up covers all clauses.
2. Escalate to Amelia Frost for confirmation that no principal-level concessions were made. Do not seek fallback authority at this stage.
3. Issue information requests on Bluefen (consent and cl 11.3 evidence), Riverlark (payout and security), Ironquay (payment evidence and assignment), DD-005 on-costs, DD-006 status, Sandbar contracts, and the title searches.
4. Prepare our SPA and Disclosure Letter mark-up on the positions above.
=== END ADVICE ===
